about: Overview

Leaflegal charges law firms per lead. Each firm's price is agreed with it before it starts, based on the practice areas, matter types and locations it chooses and the volume it wants. The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, the firm sets its own monthly cap and can change it or pause at any time.

We do not publish a price list. That is not because pricing is secret or complicated. It is because the value of a legal enquiry varies so much between areas of law and parts of the country that a single published figure would be wrong for almost every firm that read it. A price agreed for your criteria is fairer and more useful.

about: The price per lead covers everything that goes into producing an exclusive, checked enquiry. That includes our campaigns, our enquiry forms, the checks on contact details, the paid help question, the consent record and delivery to your inbox or CRM. You do not pay separately for advertising spend or campaign management.

Clients do not pay Leaflegal anything. We tell every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to. The client agrees fees directly with your firm, and our arrangement with you does not change what they pay you.

Your arrangement with Leaflegal is a payment to an introducer, so it sits alongside your regulatory duties. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told about any financial arrangement with an introducer. Our consent wording tells every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce. Your compliance officer may want to see how the arrangement is set out in your partner agreement before you sign, and we are happy to explain it.
Price factors
On your onboarding call we talk through the choices that shape your price. Understanding them helps you set up criteria that fit both your practice and your budget.

None of these factors is hidden. We will tell you how each of your choices affects your price, and you can try different combinations before deciding. If it helps, we can set out two versions in your proposal, one with broader criteria and one with narrower, so you can compare.

Different areas of law produce enquiries of very different value. A matter that typically leads to substantial work over many months is worth more to a firm than one that is quick and low cost. Some areas are also harder and more expensive to generate enquiries in. Each area you choose is priced separately.

Within an area, the matter types you choose make a difference. In family law, contested finances and simple divorce are very different propositions. In conveyancing, a sale and purchase together is different from a remortgage. Choosing narrower, higher value matter types usually means a higher price per lead but fewer enquiries you would not want.

Coverage affects both the price and the volume. A firm covering one town will match fewer enquiries than a firm covering a region or working nationally. Filling narrow criteria can take more campaign work. Wider coverage tends to produce more matches and can make volumes more predictable.
The number of leads you want each month is part of the picture when we plan campaigns for your criteria. Volume is discussed on your call and reflected in your proposal.

about.h3: What does not set your price

about: Your price does not depend on what another firm is willing to pay on a given day. There is no bidding and no auction. It does not rise during busy periods without agreement. Once agreed, it applies to every lead that matches your criteria until you and we agree something different.

Whatever your criteria, every lead you pay for is exclusive to your firm, checked and delivered with the client's consent record. Those things are not extras. They are part of every lead at every price.
Your proposal
After your call, we send a written proposal. It is the clearest way to see what working with Leaflegal would cost your firm.

The proposal is written in plain language. It should be possible for a partner who was not on the call to read it and understand exactly what the firm would receive and what it would pay. If any part of it is unclear, ask us to rewrite it.

about: Proposals often change once firms see them. A firm might decide to drop a lower value matter type, add a neighbouring county or start with a lower cap. Tell us what you would like to change and we will update it. It is better to get the proposal right than to sign something that does not quite fit.

When you compare our proposal with other ways of finding clients, look beyond the price per lead. Think about the cost of winning an instruction, the time your team spends chasing unsuitable enquiries and the management time other channels need. A proposal is easier to judge when you have a rough idea of what an instruction is currently costing you through other routes.

Once you are happy with the proposal, its terms are written into your partner agreement. That agreement sets out pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and how invalid leads are handled. Leads start only once it is signed.
Billing
How and when you are billed is set out in your partner agreement before your first lead. The points below explain the general approach so that you know what to expect.
The aim is that nothing about billing should surprise you. Everything that affects what you pay is written down before you start, and any later change is agreed with you first.

Billing is based on the leads delivered to your firm that match your agreed criteria. If no matching enquiry comes in, there is nothing to bill for. If you pause, you receive no leads and pay nothing for leads while paused.

Because you only pay for leads delivered and we stop matching once you reach your monthly cap, your cap also sets the most you will spend on leads in a month. Raise it, lower it or pause as your firm's needs change.

Your agreement sets out what counts as an invalid lead, the review period for raising one and how it is dealt with. Typical examples are wrong contact details or a lead outside your agreed criteria. A lead remains valid if the client chooses another firm or decides not to proceed.
Keep your own record of the leads you receive, when you called them and what happened. It makes it easy to check your bill against what arrived and to see which practice areas are working best.

If you raise or lower your cap, or pause part way through a month, billing follows the leads actually delivered to you. You do not pay for leads you did not receive. Any change to your agreed price, for example because you add a new practice area, is agreed with you in writing before it applies.
If something on a bill does not look right, contact our team. Because there is no platform or login, queries are handled directly by people who know your account.
Budgeting
Pay per lead makes budgeting simpler than most marketing, because the cost of each enquiry is fixed and you control how many you receive. A little planning helps you get the most from your budget.

It also helps to decide in advance what success would look like. A firm that wants to fill one fee earner's diary needs a different budget from a firm that wants to open a new office. Having a clear goal makes it much easier to decide when to raise your cap and when to hold steady.

The right budget is usually set by your team's capacity rather than by a number picked in advance. Work out how many new enquiries the people who will call leads could handle within minutes each month, and how many new matters they could take on. Your cap and your budget follow from that.

It is better to begin near the minimum and increase your cap once you are confident in your intake than to start high and leave leads waiting. Leads that are not called quickly are the most expensive leads of all.

Many firms have busy and quiet periods. Conveyancing teams may want more leads at some times of year than others. Family teams may see changes around holidays. Adjust your cap to match, and pause over closures.
If you take leads in several areas, think about each area's budget separately. Each has its own price, its own conversion pattern and its own value to your firm.

Once a month, compare what you spent with the instructions and fees each practice area brought in. Allow time for slower matters to instruct. Use what you learn to shift your cap and criteria towards the work that pays best.

Some clients bring more than one matter. A conveyancing client may later need a will or a lease extension. A business that instructs you on a debt may come back with others. A family client may refer a friend. When you judge the value of leads, it can help to think about what a good client is worth to your firm over time, not only the fee on the first matter. Track repeat work where you can.
No price list
Firms sometimes ask why we do not simply publish our prices. It is a fair question, and there are good reasons.

The value of an enquiry varies enormously between practice areas, matter types and locations. A single figure would be too high for some firms and too low for others. A range would be so wide that it would tell you very little.

Two firms in the same town taking the same practice area can end up with different prices because one wants every matter type and the other wants only the most complex work, or because one covers a single town and the other covers a whole county.

about.h3: Prices should be agreed, not assumed

about: We would rather talk to you, understand what you want and give you a price you can rely on than publish a figure that turns out not to apply. Agreeing a price in writing before you start means there are no surprises.

A published price can also hide the more important question of volume. A low price is no use if your criteria will only ever produce two matching enquiries a month. When we put your proposal together, we give you our honest view of likely volume alongside the price, so you can judge the two together.

Book a 30-minute call with our team. We will ask about your practice areas, matter types, locations and capacity, show you a sample lead and then send a proposal with your price per lead. There is no obligation to go ahead.
You can apply to become a partner firm in a couple of minutes to arrange your call.
faqs: Price per lead
How much does a lead cost?

Each firm's price is agreed with it before it starts. It depends on the practice areas, matter types and locations you choose and the volume you want. We do not publish prices because they vary widely. Book a call and we will send you a proposal with your price per lead for each practice area.
Why don't you publish prices?

Because the value of a legal enquiry varies so much between areas of law, matter types and locations that a single figure would be wrong for most firms. A price agreed for your criteria is fairer and more useful than a published number that does not apply to you. There is no obligation.
Is the price the same for every practice area?

No. Each practice area you take has its own price, reflecting the value of the work and the cost of generating enquiries. A firm taking family and conveyancing leads will have a separate price for each, set out in its proposal and partner agreement. You can add or drop an area later, and each area's price is agreed with you before it applies.
Can my price change?

Your price is agreed in writing and applies to every lead that matches your criteria until you and we agree a change. There is no auction or bidding, so it does not move because another firm is willing to pay more. If your criteria change a great deal, we will discuss whether the price needs to change too.
Does choosing narrower criteria cost more?

Often the price per lead is higher for narrow, higher value matter types or tight locations, because they can take more campaign work to fill. In return, you receive fewer enquiries you would not want. We will explain the trade off on your call. We can set out both options side by side in your proposal so you can compare price and likely volume.
Do you charge more for urgent leads?

Pricing depends on practice area, matter type, location and volume as agreed in your proposal. Many leads are urgent by nature, such as licence reviews with a hearing date. If you have questions about how particular matter types are priced, ask on your call. Your price per lead is set out in your proposal before you commit, so you will know exactly what each kind of lead costs.
Can I get a price for more than one set of criteria?

Yes. Some firms want to compare broader and narrower criteria, or different locations, before deciding. Ask on your call and we can set out the options side by side in your proposal, with our honest view of the likely volume for each. There is no obligation to choose either option, and you can adjust your criteria again later if your needs change.
What is included
What does the price per lead include?

Everything that goes into producing an exclusive, checked enquiry. That includes our campaigns, enquiry forms, contact checks, the paid help question, the consent record and delivery to your inbox or CRM. You do not pay separately for advertising spend or campaign management. Every lead is exclusive to your firm and never resold. That is part of every lead at every price, not an extra.
Is there a setup fee?

Any costs beyond the price per lead are explained in your proposal before you commit. You will know exactly what you are agreeing to before your first lead is delivered, and it will all be written into your partner agreement. If there is nothing beyond the price per lead, your proposal will say so.
Do I pay for advertising?

No. Leaflegal pays for and runs the campaigns. You pay for leads that are delivered to you and match your agreed criteria. If campaigns do not produce matching enquiries, you do not pay for them. You do not need to set a media budget, choose keywords or approve adverts. Our team handles all of the campaign work, and you focus on calling the leads that reach you.
Do I pay for leads that do not instruct?

Yes, if they are valid. A lead stays valid if the client chooses another firm, decides not to proceed or does not accept your fees. The price covers a qualified, exclusive enquiry and a fair chance to win the work, not a guaranteed instruction. Calling quickly and being clear about fees gives you the best chance of winning the work.
Is there a software or platform fee?

No. There is no platform or login. Leads arrive by email or in your CRM, and changes to your criteria, cap or delivery are made by contacting our team. Because there is nothing to subscribe to, there is no ongoing fee for software. Your costs are the leads you receive, at the price agreed in your partner agreement.
Do clients pay anything?

No. Clients do not pay Leaflegal anything. We tell every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to. The client agrees fees directly with your firm, and our arrangement with you does not change what they pay. The client is free to decide whether to instruct you after your first conversation.
Are there extra charges for CRM delivery?

Delivery to your inbox or CRM is part of how leads reach you. If your setup needed anything unusual, we would explain any cost in your proposal before you commit. For most firms, email delivery or a CRM lead email address involves nothing extra. Ask on your call if you are unsure.
Volume and caps
What is the minimum?

The minimum is 10 leads a month. It gives you enough enquiries to judge quality and how leads fit with your intake. Above that, you set your own monthly cap. Below that, results can swing a lot from month to month for reasons that have nothing to do with lead quality. You can raise your cap above the minimum, change it later or pause at any time.
How does the monthly cap work?

You tell us the most leads you want each month. Once you reach that number, we stop matching to your firm until the next month. Because you only pay for leads delivered, your cap also sets your maximum monthly spend on leads. You can change your cap at any time.
Can I change my cap?

Yes, at any time. Many firms adjust it through the year, raising it when a new fee earner joins and lowering it during holidays or busy periods. Tell our team and we will update your matching. There is no charge for changing your cap. Changes apply to the leads that follow, so you can match your volume to your team's capacity through the year.
Can I pause?

Yes. While you are paused, you receive no leads and pay nothing for leads. Your criteria and price stay the same, so when you are ready, we simply start matching to you again. Pausing is useful when your team is at capacity, a fee earner is on leave or your office is closed. It is a normal part of how firms use the service.
What if I receive fewer leads than my cap?

You only pay for the leads you receive. Volumes depend on how many people enquire and how closely they match your criteria. If volumes are lower than expected, talk to us about whether widening your criteria would help. Your cap is a ceiling, not a target. We will tell you honestly if your criteria are likely to limit volume, so you can decide whether to change them.
Can I control volume in each practice area?

Talk to us about it on your call. If you take leads in more than one area, we can discuss how your monthly volume should be split so that each team receives a number it can handle. Any arrangement is written into your proposal and partner agreement, and you can ask to change it later.
Will you push me to buy more leads?

No. We would rather you had a cap your team can handle well than a large one that leaves leads waiting. If we think your criteria could support more volume and your results suggest it would pay off, we may mention it. The decision is always yours, and you can lower your cap as easily as you raise it.
Billing
How am I billed?

How and when you are billed is set out in your partner agreement before your first lead. Billing is based on leads delivered to your firm that match your agreed criteria. Your bill reflects the leads actually delivered to you, and nothing is billed for leads you did not receive. If anything about billing is unclear, ask us before you sign.
What happens with invalid leads?

Your partner agreement defines an invalid lead, such as one with wrong contact details or outside your agreed criteria, and sets a review period for raising it. Where a lead is genuinely invalid, it is dealt with as your agreement sets out. A lead stays valid if the client chooses another firm.
Who do I contact about a bill?

Our team. There is no portal or ticketing system, so billing questions are handled directly by people who know your account. Keeping your own record of leads received makes it easy to check a bill. Raise any query as soon as you notice it, with the details of the leads concerned, and we will look into it with you.
Is there a long term commitment?

The terms, including any notice period, are set out in your partner agreement, which you see and agree before you start. You can pause at any time without ending the arrangement. We would rather firms stay because the leads are worth it than because a contract says so. Ask us about anything in the terms before you sign.
Can I see what I was billed for?

Yes. Your bill reflects the leads delivered to your firm. Because each lead arrives in your inbox or CRM with a timestamp, you can check the two against each other. If something does not match, contact our team and we will look into it with you. Keep your own record too.
Value
How do I know if leads are worth the price?

Track each lead from arrival to outcome. Over a period, compare what you spent on leads with the instructions and fees they produced, by practice area. Allow time for slower matters to instruct. Compare the cost of an instruction with what it costs you through other channels. Share results with us.
Are exclusive leads worth paying more for?

Many firms think so. With a shared lead, several firms pay for the same enquiry and only one can win it. With an exclusive lead, you are the only firm we introduce the client to. Compare the cost of winning an instruction, not just the price of a lead. Your records will tell you.
How can I get more value from my budget?

Call leads within minutes, use what the client told us, be clear about fees and follow up properly. Tell us which leads convert so we can refine your criteria. Dropping matter types that rarely instruct and focusing on those that do usually improves value. A sensible cap also helps, because leads that wait go cold.
How do I get a price for my firm?

Apply to become a partner firm and book a 30-minute call. We will talk about your practice areas, matter types, locations and capacity, show you a sample lead and send a written proposal with your price per lead. There is no obligation. The application takes a couple of minutes, and you can take your time reviewing the proposal before deciding.
Should I compare your price with pay per click?

You can, but compare like with like. A click is a visit to a web page. A lead is a finished, checked, exclusive enquiry from someone who wants paid help and has agreed to be contacted. The fairer comparison is the cost of an instruction through each route, including the management time each needs.
